minutes.headline: Select Board committed ARPA funds for an ambulance and two DPW dump trucks and heard a tax assessment investigation update.
minutes.summary: The meeting was dominated by public comment and a long board discussion of the FY23 property assessment controversy, with open friction between board members over the investigation. The board approved a liquor license transfer, a water commitment, and the first set of January 17 minutes, and committed ARPA money to vehicles. It also discussed police checks of liquor license policies and decided to stay with the status quo.

attendees.role: assistant town manager and HR director

public_comment.topic: Asked the board to approve ARPA funds for a replacement ambulance after the 2019 ambulance was damaged in a crash, citing supply-chain delays and a backup ambulance already failing twice.
Criticised the Board of Assessors for lack of public meetings and information, questioned the executive session justification, and urged a joint open meeting of the select board and assessors.
Put a series of questions to the chair about whether the assessments are correct, whether an outside assessor was hired, the DOR deadline for a redo, and the DOR caseworker.
Asked for accurate data over anecdote on assessments, noting the lack of five years of digital data and citing a property that sold well below its reassessed value.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to commit ARPA funds for a fire department ambulance and two six-wheel DPW dump trucks, as outlined in the capital plan.
A long board discussion and public comment covered the FY23 property assessment investigation, with open friction between board members.
The next update on the tax assessment investigation was set for March 7, 2023.
The board approved a liquor license transfer for a package store and the FY23 third quarter water commitment.
A majority declined stepped-up enforcement of liquor license policy sections, keeping the status quo, and tabled the January 17 second-session minutes to next week.

why_it_matters: The ARPA vote moves one-time federal money toward an ambulance and two dump trucks, which may reduce what those purchases would otherwise draw from the capital plan and the tax levy.
The assessment investigation bears on how FY23 property values, and therefore individual tax bills, are determined, and residents may be asked to weigh in on any outcome.
watch_next: March 7, 2023: the next update on the tax assessment investigation.
February 28: the next Select Board meeting, with the January 17 second-session minutes on its agenda.
